nodes.question: Why did the technology using MFCs not gain much traction despite initial interest?
nodes.answer: Subsequent proposals for using MFCs lacked clear, targeted objectives, which hindered further development.
nodes.paragraph: A brief history of BESs Luigi Galvani is regarded as the father of bio-electrochemis- try. He found that an electrical spark could cause the muscles of a dead frog to contract, and he named this phenomenon animal electricity, the force that caused the animal S mus- cles to contract [36, 37]. However, Potter discovered 1911 that adding a platinum electrode to a liquid suspension of yeast and Escherichia coli allowed the bacteria to produce electricity [13, 38]. Cohen verified this fact later in 1931 when he generated a voltage of 35 V at 0.2 mA of current using a stacked bacterial fuel cell system [13, 39]. Although early studies laid the groundwork for MFCs, it was not until 1963 that the technology gained significant attention. NASA proposed that MFCs could be used to convert human waste into energy during space missions, sparking initial interest [40]. Despite this intriguing application, the technology did not gain much traction, as subsequent proposals, such as using MFCs to power biosensors or self-sustaining robots, lacked clear, targeted objectives [41].

nodes.question: What technological advancements have contributed to the increased availability of micro-XCT?
nodes.answer: Advancements include scintillator-coated microscopes and improvements in X-ray sources that reduce the X-ray spot size, enhancing the spatial resolution of the system.
nodes.paragraph: In XCT, a series of radiographs are collected as a function ofsample rotation and then are mathematically recon-structed to produce a three-dimensional (3D) dataset. 34ut BE ;t /C2 u0e/COR/C1t 1 As the name implies, laboratory-based XCT sys- items can be installed as a standalone system in a laboratory as opposed to using larger facilities such as synchrotron sources. Micro-XCT, which providessub-millimeter and even sub-micron XCT to exam- line samples physical properties and morphological composition, has become more available due toengineering and technological advances. Theseadvances 35 38include scintillator-coated micro- scopes and improvements in X-ray sources to reduce the X-ray spot size, both of which increase theachievable spatial resolution of the system. The introduction of micro-XCT as a routine capability in the PIE process has enabled XCT to provide deeperinsights into fundamental material science phenomena. The laboratory-based micro-XCT at IMCL is particularly useful for quantifying voids and cracks in samples, examining internal interfaces between different structures or materials within specimens, ,measuring surface roughness, and identifying post-test sample changes in regimes spanning from the engineering scale to the microscale. When inte- grated with other examination techniques, XCT canhelp enable correlative microscopy which can provide information on a sample from the engineer- ing length scale down to the atomic level.

nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the research article regarding the Fe-Si system?
nodes.answer: The research article focuses on a hybrid update of the Fe-Si system by experimentally examining phase equilibria and thermodynamic properties using Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and High-Temperature Laser Scanning Confocal Microscopy (HT-LSCM) to improve heat management and process control in producing silicon steels.
nodes.paragraph: [10 12]The Gibbs energy of the liquid phase is formulated by the Modi ed Quasi-chemical Model (MQM)[13,14]in the pair approximation, which leads to a better description of the thermody- namic properties, especially the enthalpy of mixing, of amelt with a tendency to short-range order (SRO). [15,16] The Compound Energy Formalism (CEF)[17,18]is used to describe the signi cant solubility of Si in bcc_A2(ferrite, a-/d-Fe) and fcc_A1 (austenite, c-Fe) as well as of Fe in diamond_A4 (solid Si). The ordering contribu- tion of the bcc_B2 structure is adopted from thesplit-CEF description. [10,11]The CEF is also applied to intermediate silicides (Fe 2Si, FeSi and b-FeSi 2). [12]Other silicides with a de ned chemical composition (Fe 5Si3 anda-FeSi 2) are treated as stoichiometric compounds. Finally, a hybrid approach[19]is used to critically evaluate fundamental thermodynamic information with a comprehensive plant data analysis from voestalpineStahl GmbH in Linz, to approximate the heat evolution during ladle re ning of silicon steels due to the addition of ferroalloys.
